title: Prakash v. New India Assurance
text: The complainant, Prakash, filed a consumer complaint against the insurance company for repudiation of his fire insurance claim. The complainant's factory suffered fire damage and he submitted a claim for Rs 35,00,000. The insurance company repudiated the claim alleging deliberate arson. The NCDRC examined the fire brigade report and police investigation. No case of arson was proved. The repudiation of a genuine claim amounts to deficiency in service under the Consumer Protection Act. The complainant is entitled to the insured amount. The NCDRC directs the insurance company to pay Rs 35,00,000 as claim amount with 12% interest from the date of repudiation. Additional compensation of Rs 2,00,000 for mental agony is awarded. The complainant's case is fully proved.
